why_use_this: Reach for this package whenever a problem is phrased in terms of points, lines, polygons, or planes in 2D/3D space -- distance between points, whether two segments cross, a polygon's area/centroid, the convex hull of a point set, the plane through three points -- rather than in terms of abstract vectors/matrices ([vani-matrix](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-matrix)) or symbolic expressions ([vani-symbolic](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-symbolic)). `Point2D`, `Point3D`, and `Plane` are plain `f64`-only structs with no heap-owning fields, so they're freely copyable -- no `ref`/`mut ref` ceremony for individual points, only for the `Vec<Point2D>` collection-taking functions (`convex_hull`, `polygon_area`, `closest_pair_distance`, ...). Every algorithm here is the simplest textbook-correct choice rather than the asymptotically optimal one (`convex_hull` and `closest_pair_distance` are \( O(n^2) \), not the \( O(n \log n) \) divide-and-conquer versions) -- fine at this library's intended modest input sizes; reach elsewhere if you specifically need to scale to very large point sets.

math_notes.point2d_distance: \( \lVert b - a \rVert = \sqrt{(b_x-a_x)^2 + (b_y-a_y)^2} \) -- the Euclidean distance between two points.
math_notes.vec2d_dot: \( a \cdot b = a_x b_x + a_y b_y \) -- also equals \( \lVert a \rVert \lVert b \rVert \cos\theta \), the basis for `vec2d_angle_between`.
math_notes.vec2d_cross: \( a \times b = a_x b_y - a_y b_x \) -- the 2D "cross product" scalar (the z-component of the 3D cross product for vectors with no z-component); its sign tells you whether \( b \) is counter-clockwise (\(>0\)) or clockwise (\(<0\)) from \( a \), the basis for `segments_intersect`, `triangle_area`, and the convex-hull turn test.
math_notes.vec2d_normalize: \( \hat{a} = a / \lVert a \rVert \) -- the unit vector in \( a \)'s direction.
math_notes.vec2d_angle_between: \( \theta = \arccos\!\left(\dfrac{a \cdot b}{\lVert a \rVert \lVert b \rVert}\right) \), the angle between two vectors from the dot-product identity \( a\cdot b = \lVert a\rVert\lVert b\rVert\cos\theta \), always in \( [0,\pi] \) (unsigned -- doesn't distinguish clockwise from counter-clockwise; use `vec2d_cross`'s sign for that).
math_notes.vec3d_dot: \( a \cdot b = a_x b_x + a_y b_y + a_z b_z \).
math_notes.vec3d_cross: \( a \times b = (a_y b_z - a_z b_y,\ a_z b_x - a_x b_z,\ a_x b_y - a_y b_x) \) -- a vector perpendicular to both \( a \) and \( b \), with magnitude \( \lVert a\rVert\lVert b\rVert\sin\theta \) equal to the area of the parallelogram they span. Used by `plane_from_points` to find a plane's normal.
math_notes.line2d_point_distance: The perpendicular distance from point \( p \) to the INFINITE line through \( p_1, p_2 \): \( \dfrac{| (p_2-p_1) \times (p-p_1) |}{\lVert p_2-p_1 \rVert} \), the 2D cross-product magnitude divided by the line's length -- contrast with `segment_point_distance`, which clamps to the finite segment's endpoints.
math_notes.segment_point_distance: The distance from \( p \) to the closest point on the finite SEGMENT \( [p_1,p_2] \): projects \( p \) onto the line through \( p_1,p_2 \), clamps the projection parameter \( t \) to \( [0,1] \) so the closest point can't fall outside the segment, then returns the distance to that clamped point -- the segment analog of `line2d_point_distance`.
math_notes.polygon_area: The shoelace formula for a simple polygon: \( \tfrac{1}{2} \left| \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \big(x_i y_{i+1} - x_{i+1} y_i\big) \right| \) (indices mod \( n \)) -- the same cross-product idea `triangle_area` uses, summed around every edge.
math_notes.polygon_perimeter: \( \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \lVert p_{i+1} - p_i \rVert \) (indices mod \( n \)) -- sum of every edge's length via `point2d_distance`.
math_notes.polygon_centroid: The AREA centroid (not the simple average of vertices, which differs for non-regular polygons): \( C_x = \dfrac{1}{6A}\sum (x_i+x_{i+1})(x_iy_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i) \), \( C_y = \dfrac{1}{6A}\sum (y_i+y_{i+1})(x_iy_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i) \), where \( A \) is the signed area from the shoelace formula.
math_notes.circumcenter: The center of the unique circle passing through all three of \( p_1, p_2, p_3 \) -- the point equidistant from all three, found as the intersection of any two of the triangle's perpendicular bisectors.
math_notes.circumradius: \( R = \dfrac{abc}{4K} \), where \( a,b,c \) are the triangle's three side lengths and \( K \) is its area (`triangle_area`) -- the radius of the circle `circumcenter` finds the center of.
math_notes.conic_classify: Classifies \( Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + \ldots = 0 \) by the sign of its discriminant \( B^2 - 4AC \): negative is an ellipse, zero is a parabola, positive is a hyperbola -- the standard conic-section discriminant test.
math_notes.plane_from_points: The plane \( n_x x + n_y y + n_z z + d = 0 \) through three non-collinear points, with normal \( \mathbf{n} = (p_2-p_1) \times (p_3-p_1) \) (via `vec3d_cross`) and \( d = -\mathbf{n}\cdot p_1 \) chosen so \( p_1 \) satisfies the plane equation.
math_notes.point_plane_distance: The signed perpendicular distance from point \( p \) to a plane \( n_xx+n_yy+n_zz+d=0 \): \( \dfrac{n_x p_x + n_y p_y + n_z p_z + d}{\lVert \mathbf{n} \rVert} \) -- positive on one side of the plane, negative on the other, zero exactly on it.
math_notes.line3d_distance: The shortest distance between two skew (non-intersecting, non-parallel) 3D lines, each given as a point plus direction \( (p_1,d_1) \) and \( (p_2,d_2) \): \( \dfrac{\big| (p_2-p_1)\cdot(d_1\times d_2) \big|}{\lVert d_1\times d_2 \rVert} \) -- the component of the vector between the two lines' points along the common perpendicular direction \( d_1\times d_2 \).
math_notes.triangle_angle: The law of cosines, solved for the angle opposite side \( c \): \( C = \arccos\!\left(\dfrac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2ab}\right) \), given all three side lengths \( a,b,c \).
